Jermaine Johnson

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, South Carolina · Open seat

South Carolina state representative; former professional basketball player

Jermaine Johnson is a Democratic member of the South Carolina House of Representatives from Richland County. He first won his House seat in 2020. He announced his run for governor in October 2025 and won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 58.2% of the vote, beating Billy Webster and Mullins McLeod, and Sam Skardon is his running mate.

Where Johnson stands

Affordability and taxes
Proposes making housing more affordable, eliminating property taxes, and giving tax breaks to small businesses. He says affordability will be the top issue in the election.
Workforce and technical education
Proposes more state investment in technical schools to train workers.
Education and school vouchers
Opposes vouchers or other public money for private schools until public education is fixed. Supports equitable funding for public schools and a full audit of K-12 public education.
Abortion
Supports protecting women's reproductive rights and says medical decisions are best left to families and their doctors.
Roads and infrastructure
Wants the SC Department of Transportation audited before it gets more money. Proposes restructuring the agency and returning some state roads to local governments.
Data centers
Supports a statewide moratorium on data centers until legislation addresses the resources they use. He says they provide few jobs.
Medicaid expansion
Said in a June 2026 primary debate that South Carolina should expand Medicaid eligibility.
Medical marijuana
Said in a June 2026 primary debate that South Carolina should legalize medical marijuana.

Background

  • Won the 2026 Democratic primary for governor with 58.2% of the vote
  • Professional basketball player, 2009–2015, including in the NBA's minor league (Reno Bighorns) and in Mexico
  • B.A., College of Charleston, where he was basketball team captain
  • M.S., Strayer University; DBA, Northcentral University
  • Grew up in Hopkins, South Carolina
